title: There Is No Police: The GLMZ's Enforcement Landscape
body:
There Is No Police: The GLMZ's Enforcement Landscape

A plain-language explainer produced by the Gray Zone Community Advocacy Collective.

---

THE BASIC FACT

There is no police force in the Great Lakes Metropolitan Zone.

There is no institution with a public mandate to investigate crime, protect citizens, or enforce law neutrally on behalf of the Zone's population. This is not a failure of governance that is being corrected. It is the current, stable, intended state of affairs, and has been since the last unified enforcement attempt collapsed in 2208.

All enforcement in the GLMZ is done by corponations, for corponations. If a crime harms a corponation's interests or assets, that corponation's security division responds. If a crime harms only individuals with no corporate affiliation — residents of ungoverned zones, Tier 1 citizens in the the Gray Zone districts, people who fall between jurisdictions — no institution is tasked with responding. The response, if any, comes from whoever has a stake in the outcome.

---

HOW IT CAME TO BE: A SHORT HISTORY OF FAILED ATTEMPTS

The GLMZ has tried, four times, to establish a unified civilian police force. Every attempt failed. What replaced each attempt was worse than what preceded it.

ATTEMPT 1 — The Consolidated Public Safety Authority (CPSA), 2141–2158 The CPSA was the first GLMZ-wide enforcement body, established by the original Zone Charter as a condition of the municipal merger that created the GLMZ. It was underfunded from inception — corponations that had their own security divisions objected to a parallel public authority and lobbied against its budget at every cycle. By 2150, 70% of CPSA funding came from corporate licensing fees rather than municipal tax. By 2155, the CPSA was responding to corporate-filed complaints at a rate fourteen times higher than citizen-filed complaints. By 2158, the CPSA was operationally indistinguishable from a contract security firm that happened to have public charter status. It was dissolved by legislative vote, having failed to justify its administrative overhead compared to simply contracting Arcturus directly.

ATTEMPT 2 — The Zone Public Order Commission (ZPOC), 2164–2179 The ZPOC was designed specifically to avoid the CPSA's funding problem by granting it independent levy authority — the ability to assess corponations directly for public safety funding regardless of legislative approval. The corponations challenged this in the GLMZ Arbitration Court. The challenge was decided in the corponations' favor in 2171. Stripped of independent revenue, the ZPOC lasted eight more years on diminishing appropriations before being wound down. Its final annual report documented 4,200 officer positions unfilled due to inability to compete with corporate security compensation packages.

ATTEMPT 3 — The Meridian Public Department (Meridian PD), 2181–2208 The Meridian PD was the most sustained attempt and the most damaging failure. Unlike its predecessors, it managed to recruit and retain personnel by accepting corporate secondment arrangements — corporations would place their own security employees in Meridian PD uniforms for tours of two to four years, maintaining their corporate salary and benefits. This solved the compensation problem. It created a different one.

By 2190, the majority of Meridian PD officers were corporate secondments. Their primary loyalty was to their originating employer, not to the Department. They prioritized cases that served their corporation's interests. They shared intelligence with their home security divisions. They declined to investigate cases against corporate actors when those actors were affiliated with their employer. Internal review documented the problem in 2194. The documentation was classified. The practice continued.

In 2205, three separate investigations by competing corponations revealed that Meridian PD officers from different corporate secondment pools had been actively sabotaging each other's cases and selectively leaking case files to corporate intelligence divisions. The Department had become, in effect, a proxy arena for corporate intelligence warfare conducted under public-authority cover. Its neutral-enforcement mandate was entirely fictional.

The Meridian PD was dissolved in 2208. Arcturus Defense Solutions acquired its remaining assets, absorbed approximately 60% of its former personnel into the Arcturus Civil Security Division, and signed a zone-wide enforcement contract with the GLMZ Legislative Council that remains in effect. The remaining 40% of former Meridian PD personnel dispersed into corporate security divisions, private contracting, or the gray market.

ATTEMPT 4 — The Corponation Security Compact Joint Enforcement Protocol (CSCJEP), 2212–ongoing The CSCJEP is not a police force. It is an agreement between fourteen GLMZ corponations to share enforcement intelligence and provide mutual assistance in cross-jurisdictional security situations. It has a liaison office. It does not have officers. It does not accept citizen complaints. It is mentioned here because it is sometimes described in press materials as a 'joint public safety initiative,' which is accurate only if 'public' means 'the corponations that signed the compact.'

---

WHO RESPONDS NOW

Depending on where you are and what happened to you, the following entities may or may not respond:

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS — CIVIL SECURITY DIVISION The closest thing to a general enforcement force in the GLMZ. Operates under contract with the Legislative Council to provide baseline enforcement across the Zone. Contract is structured by incident type: Arcturus responds to Tier 3+ crime reports within their contracted zones, critical infrastructure threats, and cross-corponation incidents requiring neutral adjudication. Tier 1 and 2 citizen crime reports are triaged by a contracted intake system; most are not acted upon within any timeframe that has value to the reporting party. Arcturus Civil Security is not neutral — it is a corponation, with corponation interests and a corponation chain of command. The contract provides cover. It does not change the structure.

CORPONATION SECURITY DIVISIONS Every significant corponation operates its own security force with authority to detain, investigate, and enforce within the corponation's sovereign territory and against threats to its assets. Jurisdiction stops at the edge of their territory. A crime that crosses from Tessera sovereign space into ungoverned district is, at the boundary, no longer Tessera's problem. What happens next depends on whether Tessera's interest extends past the line.

NOBODY In the the Gray Zone districts, the ungoverned zones, the refugee integration areas, and the industrial ruins, enforcement is provided by nobody. Disputes are resolved by whoever has enough power to resolve them. The gangs, the community organizations, the local strongmen, the ward bosses, and the neighbors are the enforcement system. This is not lawlessness in the sense of chaos — it has its own structure and its own rules. It is lawlessness in the sense that the formal law does not reach it, and the people who live there know it does not reach them, and they have built their lives accordingly.

---

WHAT THIS MEANS IN PRACTICE

If you are a Tier 3 or higher employee of a corponation that holds GLMZ Civil Security contract space, and you are the victim of a crime in that space, you may receive a response within an hour. The response will be professional. The investigation will proceed. The outcome is not guaranteed but the process is real.

If you are a Tier 1 resident of an ungoverned district, you have three options: handle it yourself, ask your community to handle it on your behalf, or file a report through the Arcturus intake system and wait an indeterminate period for a triage decision that may result in no action. Most Tier 1 residents are aware of this. Most Tier 1 residents have never used the intake system.

This is not described as a crisis in GLMZ legislative documentation. It is described as 'a resource-appropriate allocation of enforcement capacity given the Zone's decentralized governance structure.' The phrase was coined by a GLMZ Legislative Council communications office in 2215. It has not changed.
